title: Micro-immersion 7d/30d role launch slate
content:
Purpose:
Quick, repeatable playbook for bringing new individual contributors live in weeks rather than quarters. Designed for ICs across eng/product/solutions where we want a consistent signal set: 7-day micro-immersion to unblock contributors + a 30-day capability review that informs a 90-day activation plan.

Scope / when to use:
- Use for hires (new full-time, re-hires, internal moves) where role is execution-heavy and requires early cross-team calibration.
- Not for long-term leadership hires (pm-ld, director).

Before Day 0 (owner: hiring manager + buddy):
- Confirm three measurable 30-day outcomes (deliverable, doc, or metric). e.g., "land first end-to-end demo", "complete infra onboarding ticket and smoke test".
- Assign primary buddy and mentor (buddy = day-to-day integrator; mentor = 1:bi-weekly career coach).
- Create welcome GH issue that lists access tasks + first-7 checklist and tag eng-onboard.
- Share first-week goal doc with candidate during offer acceptance (sets expectations).

Day 0 checklist (must do):
- Desk/WFA access, KMS token access request submitted, Slack invites, SSO verified.
- Short intro thread in team channel + 15-min intro sync scheduled with manager.

Days 1–3: Orientation sprint
- 30/60/90 quick 1-pager review (manager + hire) — rewrite into the hire's words.
- Shadow session(s): 2x 45-min sessions with buddy touching core repo + runbook.
- Fast-fail ticket: pick a narrow bug or doc edit that should be merged within 48h.
- Quick wins list: 3 low-risk items that show progress.

Days 4–7: Micro ownership loop
- Deliver fast-fail ticket and get PR merged.
- Demo 10-min show-and-tell to team; capture feedback in issue.
- Week-1 retro: manager + hire + buddy (15–30m) — did we remove onboarding blockers?

30-day focus areas (outcomes we grade):
- Technical baseline: can run, test, and debug the primary service locally or in staging.
- Product flow understanding: can describe the main customer flow and where this role impacts latency/cost reliability.
- Cross-team collaboration: has shipped at least one dependency or coordinated a rollout with another team.
- Documentation: contributed at least two permanent docs (runbook, FAQ, design note).

Interview / evidence rubric (used by hiring manager + tech lead to score handoff & final offer calibration):
- Areas (score 1–5, 5 = strong evidence): Core execution (deliverable velocity), System literacy (architecture + debugging), Communication (async + sync), Ownership (drives issues to close), Learning agility (picks up infra + stacks).
- Evidence types: merged PRs within first week, demo quality, peer feedback, onboarding ticket closure time, mentor sign-off.
- Passing threshold for green hire: average >= 3.5 with no area below 3.

Sample interview probes to map to rubric (for internal re-hire review / shadow debrief):
- "Walk me through a recent bug you fixed end-to-end — how did you find the root cause and validate the fix?" -> maps to System literacy + Execution.
- "Describe a time you disagreed on a rollout approach; how did you escalate or resolve it?" -> Ownership + Communication.
- Short pairing test: 45m pairing to add a small feature or fix; goal is at least one test + green CI.

Mentor + buddy protocol:
- Buddy: daily check-ins first week, then every other day weeks 2–4. Responsible for repo tours, short pairing sessions, and helping with access tickets.
- Mentor: weekly 1:1 in months 1–3, focus on career signals and cross-team context.
- If buddy/mentor not available by Day 0, escalate to people-ops ops-slate (people-ops@redwood.com).

Signals & lightweight telemetry to collect (manager):
- PR merge lag (time from opening to merge) for first 3 PRs.
- Onboarding blocker log: list of access tickets and time-to-resolution.
- Demo feedback summary (2–3 bullets).

Week-1 retro template (fill in in GH issue):
- What went well
- Blockers we removed
- Top 3 priorities for next 30 days

30-day capability review (manager + mentor + hiring panel):
- Brief 15-min presentation by hire: what they shipped, what they learned, next priorities.
- Panel uses rubric scores + qualitative notes.
- Outcome options: Green (ontrack), Yellow (needs support — create 30d growth plan), Red (offboard/role mismatch conversation).

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Should we make a standard fast-fail ticket template in GH to ensure comparable signal? (todo: PR template draft in hr-templates repo).
- How explicit should compensation/expectation doc be for internal moves vs external hires?
- Consider auto reminders in calendar for week-1 retro and 30-day presentation.

Appendix: quick templates (paste into GH issue):
- Welcome issue title: "Welcome — <name> — first-week checklist"
- Fast-fail ticket prompt: "Small, self-contained change that exercises local dev + CI and can be code-reviewed within 48h."
- Mentor sign-off blurb: "I confirm <name> has demonstrated baseline competency in running and debugging the primary service and has coherent next steps."

If this playbook looks good, I will:
- Draft a PR to hr-templates with the fast-fail ticket template + week-1 retro issue body.
- Schedule 2x office-hours for hiring managers to walk through the rubric in Dec.

-- Aisha K. (draft)
